title: In-flight steering and tier-eviction rollback playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket captures the design and runbook for an in-flight steering and tier-eviction strategy to handle model variant incompatibility, region failure, and tiered capacity exhaustion during rollouts. The goal is to provide a clear, automated decision path for runtime routing when a deployment crosses degradation thresholds, and to define safe auto-rollback and graceful degradation actions that preserve session continuity where possible.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic routing policy implemented that can: steer partial traffic mid-request to compatible replica pools, evade overloaded tiers, and execute staged eviction to lower-cost variants without data loss
A set of automated rollback triggers implemented and covered by unit/integration tests (error_rate, p95_latency, output-regression score, KV-cache-miss-impact)
Runbook steps documented and validated in a simulated chaos test that includes region outage and tier throttling
Console shows per-route decisions and an audit trail for every automated steering/eviction/rollback operation
plan: Week 1: Create compatibility signatures for model variants (IO schema, tokenizer fingerprint, KV-cache shape) and publish a variant compatibility API
Week 2: Implement steering layer that can splice routing per-request using trace id; add half-open probes for candidate variants
Week 3: Add capacity-tier heuristics (burst budget, reserved pool headroom) and eviction policy to move traffic to fallback variants by priority list
Week 4: Define and implement auto-rollback rules with hysteresis and cooldown windows; wire metrics, alerting, and audit logging
Week 5: Chaos test: simulate regional health spike and tier exhaustion; validate rollback playbook and manual override path
design_decisions: Steering vs full re-route: prefer in-flight steering for idempotent, short requests to reduce user-visible disruption; full route switch for long-running or stateful sessions
Compatibility checks: rely on a small deterministic signature (tokenizer_id + named inputs + kv-cache-dim) to avoid expensive warmups before routing traffic
Rollback triggers: combine multiple signals (error_rate > 2% sustained 3m, p95 latency > 2x baseline, output_regression_score delta > 0.08) with majority voting to avoid flapping
Eviction ordering: prefer quantized smaller models with identical tokenizer over cross-arch fallbacks; preserve session model affinity for conversational threads when possible
risks: Partial steering could expose users to mixed-model outputs in a session; mitigation: tag responses with model_version and introduce response-merge heuristics in client
False positives in compatibility signature leading to misrouting; mitigation: expand probe sampling and add warm-start budget per variant
Rollback oscillation if metrics are noisy; mitigation: add cooldown windows, and require manual confirmation for repeated rollbacks within 60 minutes
implementation_notes: Routing component will be a middleware stage in the runtime dispatcher with a small state machine (NORMAL -> DEGRADED -> EVICTING -> ROLLBACK)
Add a short-lived 'probe' token that boots candidate variants with a cached KV snapshot to measure real response divergence before ramping traffic
Telemetry: emit route_decision, rollback_reason, pre_steer_probe_score, eviction_target as structured tags so Console can filter and visualize
We will reuse existing rate-limit/burst tokens for headroom accounting and extend snapshot store to support cross-variant warm-starts
runbook_steps: 1) Detection: Alert fires for combined signal (error_rate + latency + regression) on new deployment
2) Automatic mitigation: Enter DEGRADED state and start 5% shadowing to known-good variant while sending 1% probe traffic to candidate fallback
3) If probes show <0.05 regression and headroom exists, start staged eviction (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with 5-minute pauses and monitoring
4) If combined signals persist after eviction stage 2, trigger ROLLBACK to last healthy model and mark deployment candidate as quarantined
5) Post-incident: collect traces, model outputs, and run eval suite against saved prompts; open a follow-up ticket for root-cause analysis
manual_override: Console button: Force rollback (requires 2 approvers for production deployments)
Safe-mode toggle: disable auto-eviction for a single deployment (retains manual steering only)
Emergency routing: shift 100% of traffic to regional warm pool via CLI command 'redwoodctl steer --pool warm-nyc-1'
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for compatibility signature matcher and steering state machine
Integration test that runs a simulated canary and injects latency/error faults to assert rollback within SLA
E2E chaos job in staging: region failover and tier exhaustion scenarios run nightly for 2 weeks
